title: Persona: Ingmar Bergman’s stone-cold classic
gist: Paul Lay's short culture roundup recommends Bergman's Persona (1965/66) as inexhaustible, Elif Shafak's Flaubert novel In One Brief Moment All Eternity, and Kristian Bezuidenhout's Mozart piano concerto recordings. Light, recommendation-style content with no investment-relevant claims.

insights.claim: Persona's story is simple: actress Elisabeth Vogler (Liv Ullmann) goes mute mid-performance of Electra and is assigned a nurse, Alma (Bibi Andersson), who talks constantly until the two personalities intertwine against a landscape of sand, rock and water.
insights.speaker: Paul Lay
insights.so_what: Plot summary for a canonical arthouse film.

insights.claim: Lay judges Persona to have the greatest opening sequence in cinema and says it remains inexhaustible, intimate, stark and compelling more than 60 years on.
insights.speaker: Paul Lay
insights.so_what: Signals continuing canonical status of the film.
insights.quote: It has the greatest opening sequence in cinema
insights.locator: I first saw Ingmar Bergman’s Persona

insights.claim: Elif Shafak's In One Brief Moment All Eternity is half a chronological life of Gustave Flaubert and half told from the perspective of about 30 women in his life, real (George Sand, Delphine Delamare) and fictional (Emma Bovary).
insights.speaker: Paul Lay
insights.so_what: Describes the structure of a new historical novel recommended by the editor.

insights.claim: Lay calls Shafak's book a fine, revelatory work of historical fiction that avoided the risks of its ambitious premise, which Shafak calls 'a love letter to literature'.
insights.speaker: Paul Lay
insights.so_what: Positive critical reception for the title.

insights.claim: Kristian Bezuidenhout's emerging cycle of Mozart piano concertos with the Freiburg Baroque Orchestra is praised as one for the age, with the latest release covering K466, K175 and K449.
insights.speaker: Paul Lay
insights.so_what: Signals acclaim for a period-instrument recording cycle.

insights.claim: The D Major concerto K175 was written when Mozart was 17 and was his first truly original composition in the genre.
insights.speaker: Paul Lay
insights.locator: Mozart was 17 when he wrote this work
